# Fork only: THE list of this host's system paths every fleet job sees, read-only, one per line. The only place of
# this rule: fork-fleet-launch.sh (job_fs) gives a job's unit these paths and nothing else of the host's files (its own
# copy, the hook, resolv.conf, and systemd's own /proc, /sys, /dev and memory file systems aside), and the per-OS walls
# read this file too. A path this host does not have is skipped; a symlink here (/bin -> usr/bin) is the same symlink
# in the unit; each is one mount, without what is mounted under it. A host's own extra (a tool cache) goes in
# launch.conf's ALLOW_PATHS, not here. Never a path that holds data: /home, /root, /mnt, /media, /srv, a share.
/usr
/etc
/bin
/sbin
/lib
/lib32
/lib64
/libx32
